output.brief: The August drop came from the cooling failure, not from the contractor or the kiosks. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, was down from 4 to 19 August. Room comfort on those floors fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and overall from 8.6 to 7.4. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat. Scores for floors 6-8 recovered to 8.4 after the repair and 8.6 in early September. Of the negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates did not move, and kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores were stable. The survey questionnaire and invitation process were unchanged. So don't serve notice on Orrin, don't pull the kiosks, and don't drop the August floor 6-8 responses, which would hide a real failure. Instead, restore the deferred maintenance on both chillers, which was postponed under a budget hold. Also keep the critical spare parts on site and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Apologies and half-night credits already went to the affected guests, so a further return-stay offer is optional. The 6% rate rise may have added a little to the value-score dip on floors 1-5. That dip is small and looks much like the usual August seasonal dip, so I'd keep watching it rather than reverse the rise. I'm fairly confident in the main conclusion. I didn't collect any extra evidence because the initial evidence already settles the main question.
